title: Eflornithine replacing tretinoin in a hydroquinone + steroid triple cream for melasma: a completed split-face study, results not posted
headline: A 30-person split-face study in Singapore (Fitzpatrick III to IV) compared an eflornithine 9.58% + hydroquinone 4% + fluocinolone 0.01% cream against the tretinoin-based triple cream for 12 weeks; the study finished in July 2024 and I found no results or paper.
evidenceTier: Registry record read in full (ClinicalTrials.gov); no results posted; no publication found in PubMed
fit: Relevant to the question 'can the retinoid in a triple combination be swapped for something less irritating'. Nothing usable yet: no results, and eflornithine here is an Rx compounding question.
displaces: If it worked it could replace the retinoid component of a triple combination; it adds nothing for a routine without one.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Registry record (read in full): NCT07876323, National Skin Centre Singapore with A*STAR; 30 adults aged 25 to 75, Fitzpatrick III or IV; randomized split-face; 12 weeks; started June 2023, completed July 2024.

Primary outcomes: mMASI, melanin index by colorimeter, and physician and patient global assessments. Secondary: adverse events including contact dermatitis, ochronosis and skin atrophy. The stated aim is greater improvement and less irritation than the tretinoin-based comparator.

No results are posted and a PubMed search for eflornithine and melasma returned nothing, so there is no outcome data to judge. Eflornithine is an ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor best known as a prescription cream for unwanted facial hair (background, not from the record).
Fitzpatrick V and VI were not included.
fitLine: Concept worth watching for irritation-sparing triples; no data yet, and untested in deeper skin.

fitAxes.why: Irritation was a stated comparison, but no results are posted.
This is the proposed replacement for the retinoid in the combination.
